findings.section: Behaviour contract / P2 (the Sessions block) and Decided here (how a report is compared)
findings.summary: The Sessions block's blank lines are not pinned. The cut removes the table through the blank line after it, but in the normal case the block gets no trailing blank line; the brief pins one only for 'Sessions: no brief with runs.'. Nothing separates one brief's block from the next, and 'that command's stdout, as printed' leaves open whether the stdout's final newline adds an empty line before the closing fence. The test composes the expected block and the program prints the actual one, so two sessions can each pick a form and disagree.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/report.py:55 `out.append("")` and :126 `out += ["", "Second-review lines of the run log:"...` are the blank lines the cut removes. Without a trailing blank line, `Session records: 3, schema-valid 3.` runs straight into `- 001-verdict.json: …` (run) or `Second-review lines of the run log:` (second). P2 gives a trailing blank line only to the no-brief line.
findings.fix: Write the block once as a literal template with every newline shown: heading, blank line, ```, the stdout without a blank line before the closing ```, blank line, `Session records:` line, record lines, then (when there are denials) blank line, `Permission denials:`, blank line, denial lines. Then say the block ends with one blank line, and that consecutive briefs' blocks are separated by that same single blank line.

findings.section: Decided here / How a report is compared with its golden; Worked example P2
findings.summary: The report-golden test builds its expected Sessions block by running the same `vloop metrics <run id> --by session` the Go program runs. If that command fails on the fixture, both sides hold the same `vloop metrics exited 1: …` block, and every report-kind line passes without a session table ever printing. That failure is likely: `vloop metrics` needs a git repository, and the goldens' fixture trees under testdata/ are not one.
findings.evidence: internal/cli/metrics.go:52 `root, err := g.gitRoot()` runs before anything else in the non-workspace path. The brief never says the report fixtures are git-initialised, and gen.sh (the Python) does not need git. The only P2 line that checks the error path is a separate one ('report work on a repository where vloop metrics exits 1').
findings.fix: Say that the test copies each report fixture into a temporary directory and git-initialises it (git -C, as Constraints have it). Say the report-kind lines also assert that the composed block's `vloop metrics` call exited 0 and printed a pinned number of rows for that fixture (for example 'the run fixture: 3 rows'), so a block holding the error message cannot pass as the golden.

findings.summary: 'With the same arguments (absolute paths, as today)' is not true for every script. The working directory a user passes in can be relative: hook.sh's `dir=${1:-…}`, bypass.sh's `work=${2:-$(mktemp -d)}`, and run.sh and the others' `dir=${2:-…}`. hook.sh and bypass.sh never `cd` before calling Python, so today a relative directory resolves against the caller's cwd. Under `go -C "$top"` it resolves against the repository root, and the probe reads the wrong `copilot-argv.log`, or none.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/hook.sh:20 `dir=${1:-$HOME/vloop-copilot-acceptance}`, then :30 `python3 "$here/hook.py" forms "$dir" …` with no cd. tools/copilot-acceptance/bypass.sh:14 `work=${2:-$(mktemp -d)}` and :43 `python3 - "$d/out.jsonl"`.
findings.fix: Have P4 require every script to make its directory argument absolute right after reading it (`dir=$(mkdir -p "$dir" && cd "$dir" && pwd -P)`, and the same for bypass.sh's `work`), so the Go call gets absolute paths whatever the caller passed.

findings.summary: `Session records: <n>, schema-valid <k>.` does not say which records <n> counts or in what order the INVALID lines appear. It could mean every `sessions/*.json` in the brief's folders, or only the rows the metrics view lists (the six phases). Those differ for any record with another phase, and the test writes these lines literally.
findings.evidence: P2: 'Session records: <n>, schema-valid <k>.' then one line per rejected record. P1's rows exclude phases outside plan, work, review, second-review, gate-review and verify (internal/metrics/time.go:182-211 `default: continue`).
findings.fix: Pin it, for example: <n> is the number of `sessions/NNN-<phase>.json` files in the brief's run folders, and the record lines come in folder order, then sequence order, the same as the rows.

decisions: The reports are kept and ported to Go. Issue 88 instead said the per-session view replaces report.py's run, second and work reports. Agree: the non-session sections (verdicts, task outcomes, plan, dissents) are still needed.

Every report's session table becomes the unfiltered --by session view, so the work, verify, plan and gate-review reports now list every session of the brief, not only that phase's. The gate-review report also loses its round column. Acceptable, but say so in the README.
Record schema checks stay inside the Go program, using each record's own schema field. Issue 88 said 'from the scripts'. The rejection is reasoned (no JSON reader in sh). Agree.
by_session is added to metrics/v4 as an optional property, with no v5. Agree.

by_session also goes into the close snapshots and the driver's per-iteration snapshots, because internal/closing/closing.go:119 and internal/driver/snapshot.go:26 marshal the whole Report. Committed snapshots grow by one row per session and carry the denial texts. The brief implies this but never says it; the operator should know.
The kit is a Go program run with go run, not a vloop subcommand. Agree, per #88.

The goldens are the Python's output, regenerated in task 2's gate from the base's report.py and hook.py, so that gate (and the close task) still needs python3 on the operator's machine, though no go test does. Agree.

Small choices: # has three digits, credits shows - when absent and 0.00 when 0, turns falls back to num_turns, the denial text uses a fallback chain, and the agent shows claude when absent. All sound.
checked: facts (B36 rows, totals 5.6702516/8, minSec rounding, phases summed, export delete, refusal messages, gitRoot, script call sites, Python output paths), consistency (golden cut, @DIR@, fixtures, gates vs violations), rules (CLAUDE.md, fence anchoring for nested .vloop fixtures, .gitignore), runnability (checks after each task, task 2 gate after deletion, go -C with go 1.27.1)
